# Purgatorium (p9m)

> Self-hosted sandboxes for your team and their AI agents

Purgatorium (p9m) gives each user of a team their own Docker daemon on demand: a sandbox with Portainer, a public URL for every app, sleep when idle and wake on the next request, archive on delete. A REST API and an MCP server (at /mcp) let coding agents create, wake and deploy to sandboxes.

# Getting started

# Install

No git clone is needed: every file comes from a GitHub release, and the image carries the rest.

First check the machine; it changes nothing (give it the `HOST_DOMAIN` you plan to use):

```
curl -fsSL https://github.com/csakaszamok/p9m/releases/latest/download/check-host.sh | bash -s -- dev.example.com
```

Or download it, read it, then run it:

```
curl -fsSLO https://github.com/csakaszamok/p9m/releases/latest/download/check-host.sh
less check-host.sh
bash check-host.sh dev.example.com
```

Then, on a Linux host with Docker Engine, the compose plugin (Compose 2.17 or newer) and [sysbox](https://github.com/nestybox/sysbox) (without it no sandbox can be created: the privileged `dind` runtime is for development only):

```
mkdir p9m && cd p9m
curl -fsSLO https://github.com/csakaszamok/p9m/releases/latest/download/docker-compose.yml
curl -fsSL https://github.com/csakaszamok/p9m/releases/latest/download/setup.sh | bash -s -- dev.example.com   # .env with your domain and random secrets
docker compose up -d
```

The directory must be called `p9m`: the compose project name comes from it. For a given version, use `releases/download/v0.5.0/…` instead of `releases/latest/download/…`.

`check-host.sh` checks Docker and Docker Compose, sysbox, the address pools, ports, disk and registry access, and changes nothing (its sysbox check runs one throw-away `alpine` container); with the `HOST_DOMAIN` you plan to use it also checks the DNS records and, if `certs/` has one, the certificate. Lines marked ✘ must be fixed first, ⚠ are worth reading. Run it again in the `p9m` folder once Purgatorium is set up: it then also checks the security of its `.env` and of the host (the API port, the admin's password sign-in, default secrets, an open OIDC sign-in, HTTPS, other open ports, the firewall, automatic updates, SSH passwords), marks each problem with **!**, and lists them all again at the end under *NOT SECURE*.

`setup.sh` works in the current directory: it creates `.env` from its release's `env.example`, sets `HOST_DOMAIN` to the domain you give it and `PUBLIC_URL` to `p9m.<domain>` (`https://` if `certs/` already holds a certificate, else `http://`: run it again with the domain after adding one; a `PUBLIC_URL` you set yourself is kept), fills in random secrets, creates `data/`, `opt/`, `certs/` and `dynamic/`, and prints the admin password and token. It keeps values you already set, so it is safe to run again. Without it: download `env.example` of the release as `.env` and set `HOST_DOMAIN`, `PUBLIC_URL` and the three secrets by hand.

`docker compose up -d` pulls the released image `ghcr.io/csakaszamok/p9m`. It carries the sandbox templates and runtimes, and the files the other services read: on every `up` the one-shot `p9m-init` service copies the Sablier themes, the error pages, the registry config and `dynamic/errors.yml` from it, so they always match the running version. To work on the code, see [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/csakaszamok/p9m/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).

The stack runs Traefik v3.6 with the Sablier plugin, Sablier, a registry and the Purgatorium API. The UI is at `http://p9m.<HOST_DOMAIN>` (by default `http://p9m.lvh.me`, which resolves to `127.0.0.1`), the API also on port `8081` of the host.

An app takes seconds to open the first time?

In Chrome, *Settings → Privacy and security → Security → Use secure DNS*: with "your current service provider" each new `*.lvh.me` name can wait for a slow or filtering resolver. Turn it off, or pick a provider such as Cloudflare (1.1.1.1).

Each sandbox's files (compose file, certificates, tunnel config) live in `opt/sandboxes/<owner>/<name>/`, its archives in `opt/archive/<owner>/`; `<owner>` is `admin` or the user's sign-in e-mail.

> **Give the Docker daemon a larger address pool.** Every sandbox — sleeping ones included — keeps its own compose network until it is archived. Docker's default pools only allow about 30 networks; beyond that sandbox creation fails with `fully subnetted`. Set smaller subnets in the daemon config (`/etc/docker/daemon.json`, or Docker Desktop → Settings → Docker Engine) and restart Docker:
>
> ```
> { "default-address-pools": [ { "base": "10.64.0.0/12", "size": 28 } ] }
> ```
>
> A sandbox network needs only a handful of addresses, so `/28` subnets are enough: `10.64.0.0/12` holds 65536 of them (`10.10.0.0/16` would hold 4096). Pick a range your server's own networks do not use (see `ip route`). Changing the pools later leaves the networks made before as they are: list the old pool too, after the new one, so Docker never hands out its addresses twice.
>
> **traefik-net** is the exception: every running sandbox takes two addresses on it (its frps and socat), so on a `/28` only 4 sandboxes can run at once, and the next one starts without its tunnel (`no available IPv4 addresses on this network's address pools: traefik-net`). Give it its own subnet, outside the pools above, in a `docker-compose.override.yml` next to `docker-compose.yml` (Docker Compose reads it on its own, and it stays when you replace `docker-compose.yml` on an upgrade):
>
> ```
> networks:
>   traefik-net:
>     ipam:
>       config:
>         - subnet: 10.11.0.0/20
> ```
>
> On a server already running, the network must be made again: take Purgatorium and the sandboxes' containers down (their data stays: they wake as from a deep sleep), remove the network, and start Purgatorium again:
>
> ```
> docker compose down
> for p in $(docker ps -a --format '{{.Label "com.docker.compose.project"}}' | sort -u | grep '^p9m-'); do docker compose -p "$p" down; done
> docker network rm traefik-net
> docker compose up -d
> ```
>
> `check-host.sh` tells how many sandboxes `traefik-net` has room for.
>
> **Before exposing Purgatorium publicly**, set `ADMIN_TOKEN`, `SESSION_SECRET` and `ADMIN_PASSWORD` to real secrets (`setup.sh` does). `docker compose` does not start without an `ADMIN_TOKEN`; the `.env.example` placeholders are only meant for local dev and the e2e scripts: Purgatorium logs a startup warning while one is in effect, and refuses to start with an `https://` `PUBLIC_URL`. The direct API port `8081` listens on the host only (`P9M_API_BIND`), and OIDC needs `OIDC_ALLOWED_DOMAINS` or `OIDC_ALLOWED_EMAILS` (see [Configuration](https://csakaszamok.github.io/p9m/0.18/configuration/index.md)).

All settings: [Configuration](https://csakaszamok.github.io/p9m/0.18/configuration/index.md). For HTTPS: [HTTPS](https://csakaszamok.github.io/p9m/0.18/https/index.md).

# First sandbox

```
# Create a sandbox
curl -X POST http://localhost:8081/sandboxes \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"name": "alice", "idle_timeout": "30m"}'

# Response (abridged)
{
  "name": "p9m-alice",
  "tunnel_urls": ["alice-inner-http-echo-port5678.lvh.me", "..."],
  "registry_url": "registry.lvh.me",
  "registry_username": "alice",
  "registry_password": "...",
  "docker_access": { "host": "alice-docker.lvh.me", "state": "ready" },
  "extras": {}
}
```

Sign in at `http://p9m.<HOST_DOMAIN>` to create sandboxes in the browser or mint a personal access token for your agents.

With `"template": "portainer"` the sandbox also gets Portainer, and `extras` has its `portainer_url` and `portainer_password`.

# Configuration

Main settings in `.env`:

| Variable                                                                    | Default                                               | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| --------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `ADMIN_TOKEN`                                                               | — (required; `setup.sh` generates one)                | Bearer token with admin rights on the API. `docker compose` refuses to start without it                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `ADMIN_USER`, `ADMIN_PASSWORD`                                              | `admin`, —                                            | The local admin account of the UI; it can sign in only with `ADMIN_LOGIN=on`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `SESSION_IDLE_TIMEOUT`                                                      | `30m`                                                 | Signed out of the web UI after this long without doing anything: a click, a key (also in a browser terminal), a scroll, or opening a page starts the time again; the list's own refreshes do not. Two minutes before, a bar offers **Stay signed in**; afterwards the sign-in page, and after signing in back to the same page. A session ends after 7 days in any case. `off`: only the 7 days. Tokens are not affected                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| `ADMIN_LOGIN`                                                               | `off`                                                 | `on`: the sign-in page has the **Administrator sign-in** form (also the Hub's). Off, the form is not shown and the password is not even checked: it is an emergency door, not the everyday way in (that is OIDC with `OIDC_ADMIN_EMAILS`). Turn it on in `.env`, `docker compose up -d` (a `restart` does not read `.env`), sign in, then turn it off again. While on, Purgatorium warns at startup                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `SESSION_SECRET`                                                            | —                                                     | Signs the session cookie; a long random string                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `HOST_DOMAIN`                                                               | `lvh.me`                                              | Every address is under it: the UI, the registry, the sandbox apps (needs a wildcard DNS record)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `APPS_DOMAIN`                                                               | `<HOST_DOMAIN>`                                       | The sandboxes' app, TCP, SSH and Docker addresses under a domain of their own, e.g. `example.app` beside `HOST_DOMAIN=example.dev`: the UI, the registry and the Hub stay under `HOST_DOMAIN`. Needs its own wildcard DNS record and certificate. See [A separate domain for the apps](https://csakaszamok.github.io/p9m/0.18/networking/#a-separate-domain-for-the-apps)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| `HOST_ADDRESS`                                                              | `localhost`                                           | The host's address, put into the sandbox TLS certificates and used for the registry token URL when `PUBLIC_URL` is not set                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `UI_HOST`                                                                   | `p9m.<HOST_DOMAIN>`                                   | The UI's own address, e.g. `console.example.com` with `HOST_DOMAIN=example.com`: the sandbox apps stay `<sandbox>-<subdomain>.example.com`. Under `HOST_DOMAIN`, the wildcard DNS record and certificate cover it. Set `PUBLIC_URL` to it too, and register its `/auth/callback` with the OIDC provider. A sandbox whose apps' addresses would include it (a sandbox `console` with `console-admin.example.com`) cannot be created                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| `PUBLIC_URL`                                                                | `http://<UI_HOST>`                                    | The address of the UI as users see it; `https://…` turns on the HTTPS checks (see [HTTPS](https://csakaszamok.github.io/p9m/0.18/https/index.md))                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `USER_HOST`                                                                 | `sbx.<HOST_DOMAIN>`                                   | The users' own address, e.g. `sbx.example.com` beside `UI_HOST=console.example.com`: signing in, approving `/p9m:init` (`/activate`), the API and `/mcp` for their Claude Code, and signing in to the sandbox apps. `UI_HOST` is then the admin's: a user who signs in there is sent on to `USER_HOST` (signed in again by the provider, usually without a click), and the admin's pages on `USER_HOST` go to `UI_HOST`. The API answers on both, so a project's `.p9m` from before keeps working; new ones, the `/activate` links and the users' page name `USER_HOST`. Under `HOST_DOMAIN` the wildcard DNS record and certificate cover it; register its `/auth/callback` with the OIDC provider too. Sandboxes created before reach it by its public address; new ones through Traefik, as the UI. `off`, or the same as `UI_HOST`: off, everyone uses `UI_HOST`                                                                                                                                             |
| `OIDC_ISSUER`, `OIDC_CLIENT_ID`, `OIDC_CLIENT_SECRET`, `OIDC_PROVIDER_NAME` | —                                                     | Sign-in for everyone but the admin (see [Web UI and sign-in](https://csakaszamok.github.io/p9m/0.18/web-ui/index.md))                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| `OIDC_ALLOWED_DOMAINS`, `OIDC_ALLOWED_EMAILS`                               | — (anyone)                                            | Who may sign in with OIDC, as comma lists: domains (`example.com,partner.org`, the exact domain, not its subdomains) and single addresses (`guest@gmail.com`). With OIDC on, one of them is required: with both empty Purgatorium refuses to start, unless `OIDC_ALLOW_ANYONE=true`. Checked at sign-in and on every request: someone taken off the list (after a restart) is signed out and their tokens stop working at once. The admin is never limited                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `OIDC_ALLOW_ANYONE`                                                         | `false`                                               | `true`: OIDC without `OIDC_ALLOWED_DOMAINS` / `OIDC_ALLOWED_EMAILS` lets anyone with an account at the provider sign in and create sandboxes (with Google, any Google account); Purgatorium starts so, with a warning in its log. Otherwise it refuses to start                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `OIDC_ADMIN_EMAILS`                                                         | — (none)                                              | Addresses (comma list) that are the admin when they sign in with OIDC in the browser, as the local admin is: all sandboxes, the Overview, users, no limits, host folders. They may sign in even if `OIDC_ALLOWED_*` leaves them out. Their tokens stay a user's. Taken off the list (after a restart), their session is a user's again at once. The local admin (`ADMIN_USER`) stays                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `APPS_ACCESS_DEFAULT`                                                       | `owner`                                               | Who opens a sandbox app without a `p9m.access` label: `owner` (its sandbox's owner and the admin), `domain` (anyone who can sign in to Purgatorium) or `public` (anyone; the default before 0.12.12) (see [App access](https://csakaszamok.github.io/p9m/0.18/app-access/index.md))                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `APP_ACCESS_SECRET`                                                         | generated into `data/app-access.key`                  | Signs the app access cookies and sign-in tickets                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `HUB_ENABLED`                                                               | `false`                                               | The [Hub](https://csakaszamok.github.io/p9m/0.18/hub/index.md), the team's published apps at their own address: off unless `true`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| `HUB_HOST`                                                                  | `hub.<HOST_DOMAIN>`                                   | The Hub's address.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| `HUB_ALLOWED_DOMAINS`, `HUB_ALLOWED_EMAILS`                                 | (empty)                                               | Who may look at the Hub besides the builders (`OIDC_ALLOWED_*`): viewers, who cannot sign in to Purgatorium itself. Empty: only builders.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| `HUB_TITLE`                                                                 | `Hub`                                                 | Shown in the Hub's header.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `SANDBOX_QUOTA`                                                             | `3`                                                   | Sandboxes a user may have running at once; asleep and deep-sleeping ones are not counted; `0` = unlimited                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| `SANDBOX_QUOTA_MAX`                                                         | (empty)                                               | How many a user may have running while the server has room, above the guaranteed `SANDBOX_QUOTA` (e.g. `10`). Above the guarantee a new sandbox, or one woken, needs room to spare: every other owner must still be able to reach their guarantee (their running sandboxes hold their places already), and so must one newcomer. Waking from plain sleep takes no new place, so only this maximum counts. Nobody is ever put to sleep to make room. Empty: nothing above `SANDBOX_QUOTA`; `0`: no maximum                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| `FILES_MAX_UPLOAD`                                                          | `100m`                                                | The largest file the **Files** tab (and `PUT /sandboxes/:name/files/content`) takes, like `512m` or `1g`. Every request body is read into memory first, so this (plus 1 MB) is also the cap on any request: a larger one gets 413                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `SANDBOX_MAX_TOTAL`                                                         | `200` (`setup.sh`: the suggested number for the host) | Running sandboxes on the whole server, the admin's included. The suggested number: twice as many as can all use their full `SANDBOX_CPUS` and `SANDBOX_MEMORY` at once (2 GB of memory kept for the rest), since most idle or sleep at any moment and a full server asks people to put theirs to sleep; at most as many as the disk holds at `SANDBOX_DISK` each. `setup.sh` writes it into a new `.env` in place of the example's 200, `check-host.sh` prints it, and the admin's Overview shows it under Host resources, with a warning when the limit set is well above it; asleep, deep-sleeping and archived ones take no place, so letting a sandbox sleep frees it for everyone. When it is reached nobody but the admin can create one or wake one: the admin is never refused, but its running sandboxes take places too; `0` = no limit. Each sandbox, asleep too, keeps a Docker network until it goes into deep sleep: the host's Docker address pools must have room for them (see `check-host.sh`) |
| `DEFAULT_RUNTIME`                                                           | `auto`                                                | Runtime for new sandboxes when a request names none: `auto` picks `sysbox` where the host has sysbox installed (no privileged container) and `dind` otherwise; or name one (see [Runtimes and templates](https://csakaszamok.github.io/p9m/0.18/runtimes-templates/index.md))                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| `ALLOWED_RUNTIMES`                                                          | `sysbox`                                              | Runtimes new sandboxes may use, as a comma list, or `all`. The privileged `dind` is for development only (Docker Desktop, a laptop): `sysbox,dind` there; the development compose file (`docker-compose.dev.yml`) allows `all`. Others are left out of `GET /runtimes` and the **New sandbox** form, and a create asking for one is a 400 (so is one without a runtime when the default is not allowed). Existing sandboxes keep running, sleeping and waking                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| `SANDBOX_CPUS`, `SANDBOX_MEMORY`                                            | `2`, `4g`                                             | CPU and memory limit of every new sandbox (see [CPU and memory](https://csakaszamok.github.io/p9m/0.18/resources/#cpu-and-memory))                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| `SANDBOX_MAX_CPUS`, `SANDBOX_MAX_MEMORY`                                    | `4`, `8g`                                             | How far a user can raise their sandbox's limits; the admin can go up to the host                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `SANDBOX_MAX_IDLE_TIMEOUT`, `SANDBOX_MAX_DEEP_SLEEP_AFTER`                  | — (no limit)                                          | How long a user's sandbox may stay awake without traffic, and asleep before deep sleep, at most (e.g. `2h`, `1d`); with a limit, *never* (`off`) is not allowed either. A template's longer default is cut to it; a sandbox that already has a longer value keeps it until it is changed. The admin is not limited                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| `SANDBOX_DISK`                                                              | `20g`                                                 | Disk use above which a sandbox is flagged; a warning only, see [Disk](https://csakaszamok.github.io/p9m/0.18/resources/#disk)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| `HOST_MOUNT_ROOTS`                                                          | (empty: off)                                          | Host folders the admin may mount into a sandbox, as a comma list of absolute paths (e.g. `/srv/shared,/data/projects`): a mount's host path must be one of them or under one (`/srv/shared2` is not under `/srv/shared`). Entries that are not absolute or have `..` are ignored, with a warning at startup; `/` (the whole host) is allowed, with a warning. **A mount gives whoever owns the sandbox that host folder, as root** (read-only if mounted so), and to every app in it. Empty: nobody can add a mount; ones already there stay until the admin removes them. See [Host folders](https://csakaszamok.github.io/p9m/0.18/web-ui/#host-folders)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `LOGIN_CAPACITY`                                                            | `on`                                                  | The sign-in page shows the sandbox places on the server: taken and free of `SANDBOX_MAX_TOTAL`, with a bar (orange from 90%, red when full). The page is public, so `off` hides it; nothing is shown without a server limit. Counted at most every 30 seconds                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| `GITHUB_STATS`                                                              | `on`                                                  | The topbar links to the GitHub repo and shows Purgatorium's version, stars and forks; the admin also sees when a newer release is out (one of the running series, else a later series). The server fetches the counts and the releases at most once an hour (users' browsers never contact GitHub, and nothing about the installation is sent); `off` never asks GitHub, and the link and the version stay                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `USER_VIEW_SWITCH`                                                          | `false`                                               | No effect since 0.13.0: users have no web UI. The admin can always switch (see [Simple and Advanced](https://csakaszamok.github.io/p9m/0.18/web-ui/#simple-and-advanced))                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| `GITHUB_LINK`                                                               | `on`                                                  | `off` takes the GitHub card out of the topbar (and GitHub is never asked for the counts)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| `UI_TITLE`                                                                  | `Purgatorium Agentium`                                | The name at the top left, on the sign-in page and in the browser tab titles; `none` shows no name                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `UI_LOGO`                                                                   | Purgatorium's logo                                    | The logo next to the name and the browser tab icon, on the Hub too: an `https://` address, or an image file in the container (`.svg`, `.png`, `.jpg`, `.webp`, `.gif`, `.ico`), e.g. `/app/data/logo.png` for `./data/logo.png`, served as `/assets/custom-logo`; `none` shows no logo. Its height is fixed, its width follows the image                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| `DEFAULT_TEMPLATE`                                                          | `starter`                                             | Template for new sandboxes when a request names none. An old value such as `dind-standard` makes every create without a template fail with `Unknown template`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| `DEEP_SLEEP_CHECK_INTERVAL`                                                 | `1m`                                                  | How often Purgatorium looks for sandboxes to take into deep sleep                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `HOST_SANDBOXES_DIR`                                                        | auto-detected                                         | Host path of `opt/sandboxes` (every sandbox's compose file mounts from it). Set it only if auto-detection fails                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `P9M_API_BIND`                                                              | `127.0.0.1`                                           | Interface of the direct plain-HTTP API port `8081`: by default on the host only. `0.0.0.0` opens it to every network without TLS (tokens cross it readable): only on a trusted network. With `PUBLIC_URL` empty, docker clients on other machines get registry tokens from `http://<HOST_ADDRESS>:8081`, which needs it                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `P9M_VERSION`                                                               | the release the `docker-compose.yml` came from        | The image version to run. Pin it only to stay on a version: an upgrade with a new `docker-compose.yml` then needs it changed too                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `REGISTRY_PUBLIC_PULL`                                                      | `true`                                                | Images whose versions all passed the secret scan can be pulled without a login; `false`: tokens only                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `REGISTRY_CACHE_TTL`                                                        | `720h` (30 days)                                      | How long the sandboxes' Docker Hub cache (`registry-cache`) keeps an image, counted from its **first** download: pulling it again does not extend it, so an image is downloaded again once its time is up, even in the middle of a workshop. In hours (`168h` = 7 days); `0` keeps everything for ever (the cache only grows: watch the disk). Not in hours (e.g. `7d`): the cache does not start, and the sandboxes pull from Docker Hub directly                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |

# HTTPS

Purgatorium serves HTTPS with a certificate you copy in (no automatic issuing):

1. Copy a wildcard certificate for `*.<HOST_DOMAIN>` (ideally also `<HOST_DOMAIN>`; with an [`APPS_DOMAIN`](https://csakaszamok.github.io/p9m/0.18/networking/#a-separate-domain-for-the-apps), `*.<APPS_DOMAIN>` too, in the same certificate) to `certs/tls.crt` (PEM, full chain: certificate + intermediates) and its key to `certs/tls.key` (PEM, unencrypted). `certs/` is git-ignored.
1. Set `PUBLIC_URL=https://p9m.<HOST_DOMAIN>` and strong `ADMIN_TOKEN`, `SESSION_SECRET` and `ADMIN_PASSWORD` in `.env`.
1. `docker compose up -d p9m traefik`. At startup Purgatorium writes `dynamic/tls.yml` (the certificate + an HTTP→HTTPS redirect for every host); Traefik serves the UI, API, registry and every sandbox app on port 443.

To renew, overwrite the two files and run `docker compose restart traefik`. Remove them and restart Purgatorium (`docker compose up -d p9m`) to go back to plain HTTP.

## Trying it locally with HTTPS (e.g. on Windows)

With `PUBLIC_URL=https://p9m.lvh.me` but no certificate in `certs/`, Traefik answers with its own self-signed one: the browser says *Not secure*, and although you can click through for the pages, it refuses the connections pages open themselves — the browser **Terminal** stays *disconnected*. (`lvh.me` and every `*.lvh.me` resolve to 127.0.0.1, so nothing else is needed.) Make a certificate your machine trusts with [mkcert](https://github.com/FiloSottile/mkcert). In PowerShell:

```
winget install FiloSottile.mkcert
# winget changes PATH for new shells only: pick it up in this one
$env:Path = [Environment]::GetEnvironmentVariable('Path','Machine') + ';' + [Environment]::GetEnvironmentVariable('Path','User')
mkcert -install                     # adds a local CA to Windows' trusted roots (confirm the dialog)
cd <your p9m checkout>
New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force certs | Out-Null
mkcert -cert-file certs\tls.crt -key-file certs\tls.key "*.lvh.me" lvh.me
docker compose restart p9m traefik
```

Then close the browser completely and open `https://p9m.lvh.me` again. On macOS / Linux the same with `brew install mkcert` / your package manager, and `certs/tls.crt`, `certs/tls.key`. The TLS TCP addresses (`psql`, SSH) use this certificate too, so their *self-signed certificate* warnings go away. Firefox keeps its own trust store: `mkcert -install` covers it when `certutil` (NSS tools) is installed.

The direct plain-HTTP API port 8081 is reachable only on the host (`P9M_API_BIND=127.0.0.1`, the default since 0.14.0): keep it so in a public deployment — with `PUBLIC_URL` set, docker clients get registry tokens from `$PUBLIC_URL/v2/auth`, i.e. over HTTPS.

With an `https://` `PUBLIC_URL`, Purgatorium **refuses to start** while `ADMIN_TOKEN` or `SESSION_SECRET` is a default or `.env.example` value (or `SESSION_SECRET` is unset), or `ADMIN_PASSWORD` is while `ADMIN_LOGIN=on`. A running sandbox whose address no router matches shows "This address does not reach the sandbox" instead of an endless waiting page.
# Tutorials

# Tutorials

Step by step, from nothing to an app with a link you can send to anyone. No server knowledge needed: your coding agent does the technical part.

- **[Put your app online with Claude Code](https://csakaszamok.github.io/p9m/0.18/tutorials/claude-code/index.md)**: install the p9m plugin once, approve each project in the browser, then say *deploy this app*. The easiest way.
- **[Put your app online with any agent](https://csakaszamok.github.io/p9m/0.18/tutorials/other-agents/index.md)**: Codex, Cursor, or Claude Code without the plugin, with the `.p9m` folder Claude Code makes once, or a zip from the admin.
- **[Share your app with your team on the Hub](https://csakaszamok.github.io/p9m/0.18/tutorials/hub/index.md)**: list it where colleagues find, open and vote for it.

You need a Purgatorium account: the address your team uses (for example `https://p9m.example.com`) and a sign-in. Someone in your team set Purgatorium up; to set up your own, see [Install](https://csakaszamok.github.io/p9m/0.18/install/index.md).

# Put your app online with Claude Code

You have an app on your computer (a website, a dashboard, a small tool) and you want a link to it that works for anyone. Claude Code builds and runs it in your Purgatorium sandbox and gives you that link.

**What you need:** Claude Code (in a terminal, or the **Code** tab of the Claude desktop app), [Docker](https://docs.docker.com/get-docker/) installed on your computer, and a Purgatorium account.

## 1. Install the p9m plugin in Claude Code (once)

Open a terminal (in VS Code: **Terminal → New Terminal**; on Windows also PowerShell, on a Mac the Terminal app), paste these two lines one after the other and press Enter after each:

```
claude plugin marketplace add p9m-team/p9m
claude plugin install p9m@p9m
```

It installs the plugin for you, in all your projects. It asks for no address and no token. Purgatorium shows these lines too, once you sign in at its address.

Good to know

- `claude` not found? Claude Code is not installed for the terminal: see [Claude Code's setup](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/setup). An *unknown option* means an older Claude Code: run `claude update`.
- Already in Claude Code? The same two lines there are `/plugin marketplace add p9m-team/p9m` and `/plugin install p9m@p9m`. (The Claude Code panel in VS Code has no `/plugin`: use the terminal.)

You install the plugin once. Each project then gets its sandbox in the next step.

## 2. Get a sandbox for your project folder (once per folder)

A sandbox is your own small server: your app runs there, not on your computer. You get it from Claude Code; Purgatorium's web page is only for approving.

1. Open your app's folder in Claude Code: start `claude` in that folder, or open the folder in VS Code or the desktop app.

1. Type this into Claude Code, with your Purgatorium's address, and press Enter:

   ```
   /p9m:init https://p9m.example.com
   ```

1. Claude Code answers with a link and a code, for example:

   > Open **https://p9m.example.com/activate?code=TGMH-BSGQ** and approve the code **TGMH-BSGQ**.

1. Open the link in your browser and sign in. The page shows the code and what Claude Code asks for: *a new sandbox*. Check that the code is the same one Claude Code printed, then click **Create and approve**. Creating it takes up to a minute.

1. The page then shows another code, for example `KPRW-DMXT`. Copy it, paste it into Claude Code and press Enter. Claude Code says the folder is connected, and the sandbox's name (like `k3x9q2`). That is all.

Approve only your own code

Approve a code only if you just ran `/p9m:init` yourself and Claude Code shows that same code. If someone sends you a link like this, do not approve it, and never give anyone the code the page shows after **Approve**: whoever has it gets into your sandbox. Click **Deny** instead.

What happened behind the scenes: Claude Code got a token for this one sandbox and the sandbox's Docker keys, and wrote them into a `.p9m` folder in your project. You never see or copy them. The folder is secret, and it keeps itself out of git on its own: leave it there. The token works for 90 days (then run `/p9m:init` again with the sandbox's name, see below).

If something goes wrong

- **The code ran out:** it works for 10 minutes and only once. Run the same `/p9m:init` line again for a new code.
- **You clicked Deny by mistake:** run `/p9m:init` again.
- **A wrong code pasted:** Claude Code asks again; after 5 wrong ones, run `/p9m:init` again.
- **The sandbox could not be created:** the page says why, often that you have as many sandboxes running as you may. Let one sleep (*let my other sandbox sleep*, in its project folder) and click **Create and approve** again.
- **The folder was connected to another sandbox already:** Claude Code asks before it replaces that connection.

## 3. Deploy

In the same folder, say in your own words:

> Deploy this app.

Claude Code wakes the sandbox, builds your app there, starts it and checks that it answers. At the end it gives you a link like `https://shop-web.example.com` (your sandbox's name first). Open it: that is your app, and it works for anyone you send it to.

## 4. Change and update

Changed something? Say:

> Update the app.

The same link shows the new version a few seconds later.

## Good to know

- **Sleep:** when nobody uses the app for a while (30 minutes by default), the sandbox sleeps to free the server. The next visit wakes it in a few seconds: the visitor sees *waking up* and then your app. Nothing is lost.
- **Sleep later:** *let it sleep only after 2 hours without visitors* works too (*never sleep* as well).
- **It does not answer?** Ask Claude Code *why does my app not answer?*: it reads the app's logs in the sandbox. The usual cause is an app that listens only on `localhost`; Claude Code fixes that.
- **Only for you or your colleagues?** Say *make it visible only to me* (or *only to my colleagues*): Claude Code sets `p9m.access` ([App access](https://csakaszamok.github.io/p9m/0.18/app-access/index.md)), and opening the link then asks the visitor to sign in to Purgatorium.
- **Docker is needed on your computer** only for its command line: the build runs in the sandbox.

## More projects

Each folder is tied to one sandbox by its own `.p9m` folder, so different folders can use different sandboxes, even on different Purgatorium servers. For another folder, do step 2 there: a new sandbox for it. The plugin needs no new setup.

To use a sandbox you already have, add its name: `/p9m:init https://p9m.example.com k3x9q2`. The page then asks for access to that sandbox (only one of your own), and it works the same way. This is how you move a folder to another sandbox, or connect a folder again after 90 days: Claude Code asks, then replaces the connection.

A new sandbox comes from Purgatorium's default template. For another one, name it: `/p9m:init https://p9m.example.com --template <template>`.

Used the earlier plugin, which asked for an address and a token? Run `/plugin marketplace update p9m` once, then `/p9m:init` in each project.

Installed the plugin when it was called `p7y` (`/p7y:init`)? Claude Code knows that one by its old name, and `/plugin marketplace update p9m` finds nothing. Remove it and add the new one, in a terminal, in the folder where you installed it:

```
claude plugin uninstall p7y@p7y --scope local
claude plugin marketplace remove p7y
claude plugin marketplace add p9m-team/p9m
claude plugin install p9m@p9m
```

`--scope` is where you installed it (`claude plugin list` shows it: `user`, `project` or `local`); a `local` one only from its own folder. Then start Claude Code again.

More details: [Claude Code plugin](https://csakaszamok.github.io/p9m/0.18/claude-plugin/index.md).

# Put your app online with any agent

For Codex, Cursor, Claude Code without the plugin, or any agent that can run commands on your computer. Your project gets a small `.p9m` folder from Purgatorium; the agent uses it to build and run your app in your sandbox, and gives you its link.

**What you need:** the agent, [Docker](https://docs.docker.com/get-docker/) installed on your computer, and a Purgatorium account.

## 1. Get the `.p9m` folder

Users have no web UI in Purgatorium, so the folder comes one of two ways:

- **With Claude Code, once:** in your app's folder, [`/p9m:init <address>`](https://csakaszamok.github.io/p9m/0.18/tutorials/claude-code/index.md) makes you a sandbox and writes the `.p9m` folder. From then on any agent can use the folder; Claude Code is not needed any more.
- **From the admin:** they open your sandbox in Purgatorium and download its zip (**Let your agent deploy…** → **Download**), `p9m-<sandbox>.zip`, and give it to you. Save it in your Downloads.

Either way it holds a token for this sandbox and its keys: treat it like a password. Do not email it or commit it.

## 2. Hand it to the agent

Open your app's folder with the agent and say:

> Deploy this app to my p9m sandbox.

With a zip, say where it is: *Set up the p9m zip from my Downloads in this project and deploy.* The agent unpacks it into a `.p9m` folder in your project and deletes the zip. Then it builds your app in the sandbox, starts it and gives you its link. The `.p9m` folder keeps itself out of git on its own (it has its own `.gitignore`); leave it there, the agent uses it for every later update.

If the agent does not know what to do, point it to the instructions inside: *read .p9m/README.md and deploy this app to my sandbox*.

## 3. Update

Changed something? *Update the app in my sandbox.* The same link shows the new version.

## Good to know

- The folder's token expires in 90 days. Then run `/p9m:init <address> <sandbox>` in Claude Code again, or ask the admin for a new zip.
- Lost the folder or the zip, or someone else got it? Tell the admin: they can make the old keys useless (**Rotate Docker keys…**) and revoke its token.
- Sleep and wake work the same as with Claude Code: see [Good to know](https://csakaszamok.github.io/p9m/0.18/tutorials/claude-code/#good-to-know) there.

For agent builders: everything the agent does is in the [agent guide](https://csakaszamok.github.io/p9m/0.18/agent-guide/index.md).

# Share your app with your team on the Hub

The Hub is your team's showcase: a page at `https://hub.<your Purgatorium domain>` where colleagues find the apps you published, open them with one click, and vote for the ones they like. Colleagues who only use apps can sign in to the Hub alone.

**What you need:** an app already online in your sandbox (see [Put your app online with Claude Code](https://csakaszamok.github.io/p9m/0.18/tutorials/claude-code/index.md)), and the Hub turned on in your Purgatorium (ask whoever runs it; it is `HUB_ENABLED=true`).

## 1. Publish

Tell your agent:

> Publish the web app on the Hub, titled "Stock room", described as "Who took what from the stock room".

It adds labels to the app's service in its compose file and deploys again:

```
services:
  web:
    labels:
      p9m.publish: "true"
      p9m.title: "Stock room"
      p9m.description: "Who took what from the stock room"
```

Within about a minute and a half the app is on the Hub. In Purgatorium its **App ports** tab marks it **On the Hub**.

## 2. A picture on its card

> Use /screenshot.png as its Hub image.

That adds `p9m.image: "/screenshot.png"`: a picture the app itself serves (PNG, JPEG, WebP or GIF, up to 2 MB). Without it the Hub uses the page's own preview image, if it has one, or the title's first letter.

## 3. Share

Send colleagues the Hub's address. They see whether your app is running or asleep; **Open** wakes it if it sleeps. Everyone signed in can vote once for each app, yours too.

To take it off the Hub: *remove the app from the Hub* (the agent removes `p9m.publish`), or archive the sandbox.

All labels and settings: [Hub](https://csakaszamok.github.io/p9m/0.18/hub/index.md).
# Using Purgatorium

# Web UI and sign-in

Purgatorium has a small web UI (`http://p9m.<HOST_DOMAIN>`, or `UI_HOST`) for creating and managing sandboxes without the API directly, alongside the REST API.

Only the admin

Users have no web UI: they get and use their sandboxes from Claude Code ([`/p9m:init`](https://csakaszamok.github.io/p9m/0.18/claude-plugin/index.md)). A user who signs in sees only how to install the plugin; the sign-in is for approving `/p9m:init` (and for apps open only to signed-in people, see [App access](https://csakaszamok.github.io/p9m/0.18/app-access/index.md)). A user's sign-in reaches no API either: users work with tokens. What follows is the admin's UI.

The users have an address of their own, `sbx.<HOST_DOMAIN>` by default (`USER_HOST`, see [Configuration](https://csakaszamok.github.io/p9m/0.18/configuration/index.md)): they sign in and approve `/p9m:init` there, and `UI_HOST` is the admin's only.

Two ways to sign in:

- **Admin**: a local account, set via `ADMIN_USER` / `ADMIN_PASSWORD`. Signs in with the "Administrator sign-in" form, which is there only with `ADMIN_LOGIN=on` (off by default: for emergencies), and sees every sandbox (My area + All sandboxes). Everyday, the admin signs in with OIDC, from an address in `OIDC_ADMIN_EMAILS`.
- **Signed out for doing nothing**: after 30 minutes without a click, a key or a scroll (`SESSION_IDLE_TIMEOUT`), with a warning two minutes before; the header shows the time left next to the user's name; the automatic refreshes of the list do not count, so a tab left open does not stay signed in.
- **Against guessing**: an address with 5 failed admin password sign-ins within 15 minutes has to wait 1 minute, then 2, 4… up to an hour after each further failure; after 30 failed admin passwords in an hour from all addresses together, the admin password is refused for everyone until the hour is over (OIDC still works). Failed OIDC sign-ins are only logged, never counted: a callback cannot be guessed, and a room behind one address (a workshop, an office) would lock itself out with a few wrong accounts. Every refusal is logged as `[login] <address>: …`, e.g. for fail2ban. The address is the one Traefik saw; the counts are kept in memory (a restart forgets them).
- **Everyone else**: OIDC (Google or any OpenID Connect provider). Configure `OIDC_ISSUER`, `OIDC_CLIENT_ID`, `OIDC_CLIENT_SECRET` and register the redirect URI `$PUBLIC_URL/auth/callback` (and the users' address's, `https://<USER_HOST>/auth/callback`, by default `https://sbx.<HOST_DOMAIN>/auth/callback`, too) with the provider — character for character (scheme, no trailing slash), under Google's *Authorized redirect URIs*, otherwise sign-in fails with `redirect_uri_mismatch`. Google accepts `http://` redirect URIs only for `localhost`, so with Google use an `https://` `PUBLIC_URL` (locally: a self-signed `*.lvh.me` certificate in `certs/` and `PUBLIC_URL=https://p9m.lvh.me`, see [HTTPS](https://csakaszamok.github.io/p9m/0.18/https/index.md)). `OIDC_PROVIDER_NAME` labels the sign-in button (default `Google`). Signed-in users only see their own sandboxes.

`SESSION_SECRET` signs the session cookie — set it to a long random string; sessions issued under an old value stop working if it changes.

`OIDC_ALLOWED_DOMAINS` or `OIDC_ALLOWED_EMAILS` says who may sign in and create sandboxes (e.g. `example.com`): with OIDC on, Purgatorium refuses to start without one of them, since with Google any Google account would get in. `OIDC_ALLOW_ANYONE=true` lets anyone with an account at the provider in, if that is what you want. An account not on the list is told so on the sign-in page; one taken off the list is signed out, and its tokens stop working, once Purgatorium restarts with the new list. Each user may have `SANDBOX_QUOTA` sandboxes running at once (default 3, `0` = unlimited), guaranteed, and with `SANDBOX_QUOTA_MAX` more while the server has room to spare for the others' guarantees (*Running 4 / 3 · up to 10* beside **New sandbox**); asleep, deep-sleeping and archived ones are not counted, so letting a sandbox sleep frees its place, and the admin is not limited. At the limit a user can neither create a sandbox nor wake one, from sleep or deep sleep: its address shows *Running limit reached*, its address shows *Running limit reached* with the running sandboxes, and **Wake** in the panel lets the owner put one to sleep instead (`POST /sandboxes/:name/start` with `{"sleep": "<name>"}`). Purgatorium never puts a sandbox to sleep on its own.
