- **SSH:** `ssh root@<sandbox>-shell-tcp.<domain>` through port 443 ([SSH, terminal and logs](https://csakaszamok.github.io/p9m/0.18/shell-and-logs/index.md)); inside, `docker` talks to the sandbox's Docker.
- **Logs** of every app in the sandbox: `GET /sandboxes/<name>/logs/stream` (Server-Sent Events).
- **Move the work itself into the sandbox:** with the Claude Code plugin, `/p9m:teleport` puts the project, its confirmed secrets and the conversation into a `claude` container next to the apps, to continue there ([Claude Code plugin](https://csakaszamok.github.io/p9m/0.18/claude-plugin/#continue-in-the-sandbox-p9mteleport)).

## With Portainer

A sandbox made from the `portainer` template (or one with Portainer in its own compose) also has Portainer, which proxies the sandbox's Docker daemon over HTTPS: an agent can deploy through its API without the `docker` command line. `GET /sandboxes/<name>` then has:

- `extras.portainer_url`, for example `https://shop-portainer.example.com` (if its host is not in `tunnel_urls`, Portainer is published on `127.0.0.1` and private to the sandbox: ask the user to publish it on all interfaces, `9000:9000`, in **Starter stack…**);
- `extras.portainer_password` (user `admin`).

`GET <portainer_url>/api/status` returning JSON means Portainer is ready (an HTML answer is the waiting page). Portainer traffic wakes an asleep sandbox and keeps it awake.

### Sign in to Portainer

If `p9m.env` has `P9M_PORTAINER_URL` and `P9M_PORTAINER_TOKEN`, skip the sign-in: use `P9M_PORTAINER_URL` as `<portainer_url>` and send `X-API-Key: <P9M_PORTAINER_TOKEN>` instead of `Authorization: Bearer <jwt>` on every Portainer call below. (A line `# Portainer: not included (…)` says why there is none; then sign in as below, or use the Docker command line, [2](#2-connect-the-docker-command-line).)

Otherwise sign in with `extras.portainer_password`:

```
POST <portainer_url>/api/auth
Content-Type: application/json

{"username": "admin", "password": "<extras.portainer_password>"}
```

The answer is `{"jwt": "…"}`. Send `Authorization: Bearer <jwt>` on every Portainer call below.

Then find the environment (endpoint) ID. It is the sandbox's Docker daemon, usually `1`:

```
GET <portainer_url>/api/endpoints      → [{"Id": 1, "Name": "primary", …}]
```

If the list is empty (nobody clicked **Get started** in the Portainer UI yet), create the environment once:

```
POST <portainer_url>/api/endpoints
Content-Type: multipart/form-data

Name=local
EndpointCreationType=1
```

### Deploy an app as a stack

A Portainer stack is a compose project that Portainer can update later. Deploy it from compose text:

```
POST <portainer_url>/api/stacks/create/standalone/string?endpointId=1
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "name": "shop",
  "stackFileContent": "services:\n  web:\n    image: registry.example.com/shop:1.4.2\n    ports: [\"8080:8080\"]\n    labels:\n      p9m.subdomain: shop\n",
  "env": [{"name": "LOG_LEVEL", "value": "info"}]
}
```

The answer includes the stack `Id`; keep it for updates. `GET <portainer_url>/api/stacks` lists the stacks with their IDs.

The same rules hold as in [3. Deploy an app](#3-deploy-an-app): publish ports on all interfaces, set a restart policy.

### Update a stack

Change the image tag in the compose text and redeploy. `pullImage: true` pulls the image again even if the tag did not change (for `:latest`):

```
PUT <portainer_url>/api/stacks/<stack id>?endpointId=1
Content-Type: application/json

{"stackFileContent": "<the full compose text>", "env": [], "prune": true, "pullImage": true}
```

`prune: true` removes services that are no longer in the compose text. Portainer recreates the changed containers; the volumes are kept.

To build in the sandbox, send the build context as a tar archive to the Docker build endpoint through Portainer's Docker proxy:

```
POST <portainer_url>/api/endpoints/1/docker/build?t=shop:1.4.3
Content-Type: application/x-tar

<tar of the directory with the Dockerfile>
```

The answer streams the build log as JSON lines; the last line is `{"stream":"Successfully tagged shop:1.4.3\n"}` on success, or an `{"error": …}` line on failure. Then redeploy the stack with `image: shop:1.4.3` and `pullImage: false` (the image only exists locally).

### Everything else Docker can do

`<portainer_url>/api/endpoints/1/docker/<Docker Engine API path>` is the sandbox's Docker Engine API. Examples:

| Call                                                             | Docker Engine API       |
| ---------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------- |
| `GET …/docker/containers/json`                                   | list running containers |
| `GET …/docker/containers/<name>/logs?stdout=1&stderr=1&tail=200` | container logs          |
| `POST …/docker/containers/<name>/restart`                        | restart a container     |
| `POST …/docker/images/create?fromImage=alpine&tag=3.20`          | pull an image           |
| `DELETE …/docker/images/<image>`                                 | remove an image         |

The stack Purgatorium deployed when it created the sandbox (Portainer + `http-echo`) was deployed with `docker compose` outside Portainer: Portainer shows it but cannot edit it as a stack.

## Things to keep in mind

- **Sleep:** the sandbox sleeps after its idle timeout without HTTP traffic, 30 minutes by default. The user can change this or turn it off in the UI (**Sleep settings…**) or with `PATCH /sandboxes/<name>` `{"idle_timeout": "2h"}`, where `0` or `off` means never. Docker traffic keeps a running sandbox awake (a build, `docker logs -f`, a pull), but a connection that is only open does not; plain HTTP traffic to its apps (or to Portainer) counts too.
- **Archive** (`DELETE /sandboxes/<name>`, **Archive…** in the UI) archives the sandbox: its configuration and data are kept in the archive, and it is removed from the list.
- **The Purgatorium API reference** is at `<Purgatorium URL>/swagger`.
# Reference

# API

[![](../media/api-curl-poster.webp)](../media/api-curl.mp4)

| Method   | Path                                       | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| -------- | ------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `POST`   | `/sandboxes`                               | Create a sandbox (`name`, or none for a generated one like `k3x9q2`; optional `runtime` like `dind`, `template` like `starter` (its starter stack as it is: a `compose` text is refused), `idle_timeout` like `30m`, `deep_sleep_after` like `7d` or `off`, `ssh_keys` (extra SSH public keys for this sandbox only), `cpus` like `2`, `memory` like `4g`, `create_inner_stack: false` for no template stack)                              |
| `GET`    | `/sandboxes`                               | List all sandboxes                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| `GET`    | `/sandboxes/summary`                       | How many sandboxes: `quota`, `total`, `free`, `running`, `asleep`, `deep_sleep`, `archived`; your own (and `server_full`), or for the admin the whole server, `by_owner`, `server_limit` / `server_used` and `resources` (not with a token limited to one sandbox)                                                                                                                                                                         |
| `GET`    | `/sandboxes/:name`                         | Get sandbox details; the Docker client certificates and key (`ca_cert`, `client_cert`, `client_key`) only with `?include_keys=true`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| `GET`    | `/sandboxes/:name/compose`                 | The starter stack deployed into the sandbox (compose YAML), secrets masked (**Starter stack…** in the UI)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `PATCH`  | `/sandboxes/:name`                         | Change `idle_timeout` and/or `deep_sleep_after` (see [Sleep and wake](https://csakaszamok.github.io/p9m/0.18/sleep-wake/index.md)), `cpus` and/or `memory` (see [CPU and memory](https://csakaszamok.github.io/p9m/0.18/resources/#cpu-and-memory))                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| `GET`    | `/sandbox-name`                            | A free name for a new sandbox (`{"name": "k3x9q2"}`): what **New sandbox** fills in                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| `POST`   | `/sandboxes/:name/start`                   | Wake a sandbox, also from deep sleep (**Wake** in the UI); 409 at the owner's limit with `reason` and `running`; `{"sleep": "<name>"}` puts that running one to sleep first                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `POST`   | `/sandboxes/:name/stop`                    | Put a sandbox to sleep now (**Sleep** in the UI)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `POST`   | `/sandboxes/:name/deep-sleep`              | Put a sandbox into deep sleep now, also a running one (**Deep sleep now** on the panel's **Details** tab)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `POST`   | `/sandboxes/:name/keep-awake`              | Start a running sandbox's sleep countdown over (**Reset** next to *Sleeps in*); 409 if it is not running                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `POST`   | `/sandboxes/:name/export`                  | A zip for coding agents: a new token for the sandbox, its Docker client keys, a README (owner/admin; not with a token limited to one sandbox); `docker: false` without the keys, `format: "env"` the p9m.env text                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `POST`   | `/sandboxes/:name/project-link`            | A single-use link (5 minutes) to the project's `.p9m` folder with the Docker client keys, checked first; answers `url`, `command` (`curl … \| tar -x`) and `context_commands`, never the keys                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `GET`    | `/project-dir/:token`                      | The `.p9m` folder as a tar, once (no token: the link is the authorization); `410` when used or expired                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `POST`   | `/device/code`                             | Start a device approval for `/p9m:init` (no token): `sandbox` for one of the user's, or none for a new one, from `template` (or the default; not with `sandbox`; an unknown one is `400`). Answers `device_code` (the agent's secret), `user_code`, `verification_uri_complete` and `expires_in` (600)                                                                                                                                     |
| `POST`   | `/device/token`                            | Hand in the confirmation code the approval page showed (no token; `device_code` and `code` in the body): `approved` with the same answer as `project-link` and `name`, the sandbox as the user knows it (`shop` for `p9m-shop`), once; `400` `{"status": "wrong", "tries_left"}` (5 wrong ones end it), `403` `denied`, `409` `pending`, `410` `expired` (also used or ended). The approval resets the 10 minutes                          |
| `GET`    | `/activate`                                | The page where a signed-in user approves or denies a code (`?code=`): access to the named sandbox, or a new one; `POST` sends the decision, creates the new sandbox (as `POST /sandboxes`) and shows the confirmation code                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `POST`   | `/sandboxes/:name/docker-keys`             | New Docker access certificates (**Enable** / **Rotate Docker keys…**); restarts the sandbox                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `GET`    | `/sandboxes/:name/registry`                | The sandbox's images in the registry, with secret-scan results                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `DELETE` | `/sandboxes/:name/registry/:app/:digest`   | Delete one version of an image                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `POST`   | `/sandboxes/:name/restart`                 | Restart a sandbox                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `GET`    | `/sandboxes/:name/files`                   | List a folder of the sandbox's files (`path`, default `/root`): `/root`, `/home`, `/srv` and `/opt`, the folders kept over a deep sleep, and the apps' volumes; the sandbox must be running (409 `not_running` otherwise). See [Files](https://csakaszamok.github.io/p9m/0.18/files/index.md)                                                                                                                                              |
| `GET`    | `/sandboxes/:name/files/content`           | Download a file (`path`), or a folder as a tar                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `PUT`    | `/sandboxes/:name/files/content`           | Upload a file to `path` (the body is the file; missing folders on the path are made), up to `FILES_MAX_UPLOAD`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `GET`    | `/sandboxes/:name/files/text`              | A text file's content as JSON (UTF-8, up to 1 MB): for agents                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `POST`   | `/sandboxes/:name/files/mkdir`             | Create a folder (`{"path": "/srv/data"}`)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `DELETE` | `/sandboxes/:name/files`                   | Delete a file or a folder (`path`), not the four folders themselves (nor a volume's folder)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `GET`    | `/sandboxes/:name/volumes`                 | The volumes of the apps in the sandbox's own Docker: `name`, `path` (for the routes above), `project`, `containers` that use it                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| `GET`    | `/sandboxes/:name/mounts`                  | The host folders mounted into the sandbox: `mounts` (`host`, `target`, `readonly`), `enabled` (`HOST_MOUNT_ROOTS` is set); the admin also gets `roots`. Owner, admin, and a token limited to the sandbox. See [Host folders](https://csakaszamok.github.io/p9m/0.18/web-ui/#host-folders)                                                                                                                                                  |
| `POST`   | `/sandboxes/:name/mounts`                  | Mount a host folder (admin only, `HOST_MOUNT_ROOTS` set, else 403 / 409): `{"host": "/srv/shared/team", "target": "/mnt/team", "readonly": true}`, `target` defaulting to `/mnt/<last part of host>`. The sandbox container is recreated (a running one restarts). 400 for a path outside the roots or a target that is not allowed; 409 with Docker's words when Docker refuses it (e.g. the host folder does not exist), nothing changed |
| `DELETE` | `/sandboxes/:name/mounts?target=/mnt/team` | Unmount it (admin only; also with `HOST_MOUNT_ROOTS` unset); the sandbox container is recreated                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| `DELETE` | `/sandboxes/:name`                         | Archive the sandbox, then remove it (**Archive…** in the UI; see [Delete = archive](https://csakaszamok.github.io/p9m/0.18/archive/index.md))                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `GET`    | `/runtimes`                                | List the runtimes new sandboxes may use (`name`, `description`, `default`; only those in `ALLOWED_RUNTIMES` when it is set)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `GET`    | `/templates`                               | List the templates (`name`, `description`, `default`)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| `GET`    | `/ssh-keys`                                | Your SSH public keys (`id`, `name`, `type`, `fingerprint`, `created_at`)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `POST`   | `/ssh-keys`                                | Add a public key (`key`, optional `name`); it lets you into all your sandboxes with SSH                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| `GET`    | `/sandboxes/:name/ssh-key`                 | The sandbox's generated SSH private key (download)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| `POST`   | `/sandboxes/:name/ssh-key`                 | Generate it for an SSH sandbox that has none yet                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `GET`    | `/sandboxes/:name/containers`              | The containers in the sandbox's own Docker: `name`, `project`, `service`, `image`, `state`, `status`, running ones first; the sandbox must be running (409 `not_running` otherwise)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| `GET`    | `/sandboxes/:name/terminal`                | The browser terminal (page; the same path as a websocket: the shell; `?container=<name>`: in that container of the sandbox's own Docker)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `GET`    | `/sandboxes/:name/logs`                    | The logs page (signed-in browsers)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| `GET`    | `/sandboxes/:name/logs/stream`             | The sandbox's app logs as Server-Sent Events: the last 100 lines of every container, then live (token too)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `DELETE` | `/ssh-keys/:id`                            | Delete one of your keys (it stops working at once)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| `GET`    | `/templates/:name`                         | A template's `compose.yaml` as written (`compose`), to show before a create                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `GET`    | `/me`                                      | Who you are signed in as, Purgatorium's own address (`url`), your running sandboxes and limit, and `server_places`: the sandbox places on the server, `used` and `limit` (`null` without a server limit)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `PUT`    | `/me/view`                                 | The web UI's view for this account: `{"view": "simple"}` or `"advanced"` (`GET /me` returns it as `view`, and whether the account may switch as `view_switch`); a user gets 403 unless `USER_VIEW_SWITCH=true`                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `PUT`    | `/me/theme`                                | The web UI's theme for this account: `{"theme": "light"}`, `"dark"`, or `"system"` to follow the device again (`GET /me` returns it as `theme`, `null` when the device decides); any account may set it                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| `GET`    | `/tokens`                                  | List your personal access tokens (`hint`: the token's start and end, e.g. `p9m_aB3x…9fQz`; null for tokens made before hints)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `POST`   | `/tokens`                                  | Mint a personal access token (`name`, optional `expires_in` like `30d`/`90d`/`never`)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| `DELETE` | `/tokens/:id`                              | Revoke a personal access token                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `GET`    | `/users`                                   | Accounts (admin): first and last seen, last sign-in, sign-ins, sandboxes now and created, last API use                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `DELETE` | `/users/:account`                          | Forget an account's stats row (admin); the account and its sandboxes stay                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |

All endpoints require `Authorization: Bearer <ADMIN_TOKEN | personal token>` or a signed-in browser session. Users only see their own sandboxes.

## OpenAPI and clients

The whole API is described as OpenAPI 3.0 at `/swagger.json` (no token needed to read it), and you can try it in Swagger UI at `/swagger`. There is no official SDK yet; generate a client in your language from that document instead, for example typed TypeScript:

```
curl -s https://p9m.example.com/swagger.json -o p9m.json
npx openapi-typescript p9m.json -o p9m.d.ts   # use it with openapi-fetch
```

or any language [openapi-generator](https://openapi-generator.tech/) supports (`openapi-generator-cli generate -i p9m.json -g python -o p9m-client`). The document's version is Purgatorium's own, so regenerate after an upgrade.

More reading: [architecture diagrams](https://csakaszamok.github.io/p9m/0.18/architecture.html), [how agents deploy](https://csakaszamok.github.io/p9m/0.18/agent-guide/index.md), [comparison with other sandbox platforms](https://csakaszamok.github.io/p9m/0.18/comparison/index.md), [roadmap](https://csakaszamok.github.io/p9m/0.18/roadmap/index.md).

# Security

Purgatorium is built for a team that trusts each other's intentions but not each other's mistakes: it keeps one person's broken compose file, runaway container or exposed port from affecting everyone else. It is **not** a boundary against hostile code.

What it does:

- each user gets their own Docker daemon, so their containers, images, volumes and networks are separate from everyone else's and from the host's Docker;
- an app's private addresses are reachable only inside its own sandbox, and ports published on `127.0.0.1` only through its tunnel (see [Isolation between sandboxes](https://csakaszamok.github.io/p9m/0.18/networking/#isolation-between-sandboxes));
- users see and change only their own sandboxes, through the UI, the API or a personal access token; the admin sees all;
- a sandbox's web apps open only for its owner (and the admin) unless labelled `domain` or `public` ([App access](https://csakaszamok.github.io/p9m/0.18/app-access/index.md));
- with an `https://` `PUBLIC_URL`, Purgatorium refuses to start with default secrets; `docker compose` does not start without an `ADMIN_TOKEN`, and Purgatorium does not start with OIDC open to anyone (`OIDC_ALLOW_ANYONE=true` aside);
- the direct plain-HTTP API port `8081` listens on the host only (`P9M_API_BIND`): from elsewhere everything goes through Traefik.

**On every server**: install [sysbox](https://github.com/nestybox/sysbox) on the host. Only `sysbox` is allowed by default (`ALLOWED_RUNTIMES`), so nobody can create a privileged `dind` sandbox; without sysbox no sandbox can be created at all. **The `dind` runtime is for development only** (a laptop, Docker Desktop): never allow it on a server. `check-host.sh` tells whether sysbox works on the machine, and, run in the `p9m` folder, lists what else is not secure. Sandboxes that already exist keep their runtime: recreate the `dind` ones.

What it does not do:

- **Without sysbox, sandboxes run `privileged` (the `dind` runtime).** Code with root inside such a sandbox can escape to the host. That is why only `sysbox` is allowed by default, which runs Docker in an unprivileged container; Docker Desktop cannot run sysbox, so for development there `dind` is allowed (`docker-compose.dev.yml`), and Purgatorium says so at startup. Only let people and agents you would give a shell on the host run code in `dind` sandboxes.
- **`sysbox` is not a VM:** its sandboxes run unprivileged, in their own user namespace, but share the host's kernel, so a kernel exploit would still reach the host.
- There is no network policy between a sandbox and the internet, and no hard disk quota per sandbox: only a warning above its disk limit (see [Disk](https://csakaszamok.github.io/p9m/0.18/resources/#disk)); CPU and memory limits exist (see [CPU and memory](https://csakaszamok.github.io/p9m/0.18/resources/#cpu-and-memory)).
- The Purgatorium container mounts the host's Docker socket, so whoever controls Purgatorium controls the host. That is why a sandbox's starter stack is always its template's (no compose text of the user's goes through Purgatorium), and is run by `docker compose` inside the sandbox, not in the Purgatorium container; why the files Purgatorium reads and writes in a sandbox's directory are mounted into the sandbox read-only (`/inner`, and of `/certs` only its dockerd's certificate), and read and written without following a symlink; and why Purgatorium's internal port (app access for Traefik) listens only on a network no sandbox is on. Traefik's API is not served.
- A sandbox is on its own network only: Purgatorium and Traefik reach it through its frp tunnel (frpc connects out of it), so no sandbox reaches another one's ports past [app access](https://csakaszamok.github.io/p9m/0.18/app-access/index.md).
- A [host folder](https://csakaszamok.github.io/p9m/0.18/web-ui/#host-folders) the admin mounts into a sandbox (`HOST_MOUNT_ROOTS`) is the sandbox owner's, as root, and every app's and agent's in it: read-only only limits writing. Keep the roots narrow.

In short, run it for a team, on a server you can rebuild, best behind a VPN or with the sign-in limited to your domain; for untrusted code (public sign-up, code from strangers), use a microVM-based sandbox instead; a Kata Containers runtime (a VM per sandbox) is on the [roadmap](https://csakaszamok.github.io/p9m/0.18/roadmap/index.md).

Found a vulnerability? See [SECURITY.md](https://github.com/csakaszamok/p9m/blob/main/SECURITY.md).

# Upgrading

To a new version, in the install directory:

```
curl -fsSLO https://github.com/csakaszamok/p9m/releases/latest/download/docker-compose.yml
docker compose pull && docker compose up -d
```

If `.env` sets `P9M_VERSION`, change or remove it. Each release's notes are in the [changelog](https://github.com/csakaszamok/p9m/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md).

## To 0.14.0: the secure defaults

Purgatorium 0.14.0 no longer starts with open defaults. Before `docker compose up -d`, check `.env`:

- **`ADMIN_TOKEN`** must be set: `docker compose` refuses to start without it (the compose file had `abc123` as a fallback). `./setup.sh` fills in a random one; scripts and agents using the old token need the new one.
- **The API port `8081` listens on the host only.** If something on another machine called `http://<server>:8081` (a script, or docker clients getting registry tokens while `PUBLIC_URL` is empty), point it at `PUBLIC_URL` instead, or set `P9M_API_BIND=0.0.0.0` on a trusted network.
- **With OIDC on, set `OIDC_ALLOWED_DOMAINS` or `OIDC_ALLOWED_EMAILS`**, or Purgatorium refuses to start (`docker compose logs p9m` says why). To keep letting anyone with an account at the provider in, set `OIDC_ALLOW_ANYONE=true`.

`./check-host.sh`, run in the install directory, lists what is still open.

## From Purgatory (p7y)

There is no upgrade from Purgatory (p7y), the project's former name: [install](https://csakaszamok.github.io/p9m/0.18/install/index.md) Purgatorium afresh, in a new directory called `p9m`. Nothing is carried over: sandboxes, archives, users, tokens and settings start empty, and `P7Y_*` settings and `p7y.*` labels are not read.

# Why Purgatorium, and how it compares

*As of October 2026. What is said about other products comes from the public sources listed at the bottom, and can change quickly.*

## What Purgatorium is for

**A place where a team's apps run: the ones people build with AI agents or vibe-code in an afternoon.** Everyone gets their own space, every app gets a URL colleagues can open, and what nobody uses costs nothing. On your own server, not in someone else's cloud.

Think of it as **a self-hosted Vercel or Railway for the whole team**: you hand an agent a `p9m.env`, it deploys a `docker-compose.yml`, and a minute later `https://shop-web.example.com` works.

## How teams do this today, and what goes wrong

| Today                                                       | What goes wrong                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| ----------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| **It runs on someone's laptop**                             | No URL to show it, it stops when the lid closes, and it only works on that machine.                                                                                                                                                              |
| **A cloud PaaS** (Vercel, Railway, Render, Fly.io, Netlify) | Every experiment is another project on the bill; code and data leave the company network; a multi-container stack (app + database + worker) has to be rebuilt service by service; Vercel runs request-driven functions, not always-on processes. |
| **One shared VPS with Docker or Portainer**                 | Everyone is on one Docker daemon: they see each other's containers, ports collide, one runaway stack slows everyone down, one wrong `docker rm` hits someone else.                                                                               |
| **Coolify or Dokploy**                                      | Built for running a team's production apps: an admin sets up projects, everything keeps running all the time, teams on one server still share the daemon.                                                                                        |
| **A VM for everyone**                                       | Expensive while idle, and someone has to create, patch and clean up every one of them.                                                                                                                                                           |

## What Purgatorium does instead

- **Self-service, like a cloud PaaS.** Anyone signs in (Google or any OIDC) and creates a sandbox; a quota and CPU / memory limits keep one person from taking the whole server.
- **Its own Docker for everyone.** Every sandbox has its own Docker daemon: what an agent produces (`docker-compose.yml` with app, database, cache) runs as it is, and nobody sees or breaks anyone else's containers.
- **A URL for every app, automatically.** Whatever a sandbox publishes gets `https://<name>-<app>.<domain>`; databases and SSH get a TLS address on port 443. No DNS, no proxy rules per app.
- **Idle costs nothing.** A sandbox without traffic falls asleep and wakes on the next request; after a longer sleep its containers are freed. Twenty experiments, three in use: the server carries three.
- **Made for coding agents.** **Let your agent deploy…** (the Claude Code plugin with `/p9m:init`, or a zip for any agent) gives the agent a token for that one sandbox, Docker access from outside and a registry login; every pushed image is scanned for secrets before anyone can pull it anonymously.
- **Your server, your data, no bill per app.** One `docker compose up` on one Linux host, also inside a company network; no paid edition.
- **Nothing is lost.** Delete archives the sandbox's configuration and data.

## Against a cloud PaaS (Vercel, Railway, Render, Fly.io)

Purgatorium gives a team what these give one developer, on hardware the team already has.

|                                  | Vercel / Railway / Render / Fly.io                                                                                              | Purgatorium                                                           |
| -------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Where it runs, where the data is | Their cloud                                                                                                                     | Your server, also inside a company network                            |
| What you pay for                 | Every project, service and its usage                                                                                            | The server                                                            |
| What you deploy                  | Mostly one service per app (Vercel: request-driven functions, also from a Dockerfile); Fly.io's Docker Compose support is basic | A whole `docker-compose.yml`, as it is, with its own Docker daemon    |
| Idle apps                        | Railway, Render (free tier) and Fly.io can scale to zero; otherwise they run and are billed                                     | Sleep by default, wake on the next request                            |
| Many people on one account       | A team plan; everyone sees the team's projects                                                                                  | Everyone sees only their own sandboxes; tokens limited to one sandbox |
| Production features              | Global edge, autoscaling, managed databases, backups, zero operations                                                           | None of these: one host, you run it                                   |

**Pick a cloud PaaS** for an app in production that has to scale and be up at 3 a.m. without you. **Pick Purgatorium** for the many apps before that point: experiments, demos, internal tools, vibe-coded apps, test environments, and for whatever must not leave the company network.

## Against self-hosted tools (Coolify, Dokploy, Portainer)

These also run on your own server, but they are built for **one team running its apps**, not for **many people each having their own space**.

|                                             | Purgatorium                                                                  | Coolify                                                               | Dokploy                                                 | Portainer CE                                                                   |
| ------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Separation between teams on **one** server  | each sandbox has its own Docker daemon and network                           | teams get their own servers; on a shared server the daemon is shared  | a shared daemon; members get access per project         | a shared daemon; roles (read-only, operator) only in the paid Business Edition |
| What the dashboard hides, Docker also hides | yes                                                                          | no                                                                    | no                                                      | no                                                                             |
| Who creates an environment                  | anyone, within a quota                                                       | an admin or team member, in the team's project                        | an admin, or a member given the permission              | an admin                                                                       |
| Idle apps                                   | sleep                                                                        | keep running                                                          | keep running                                            | keep running                                                                   |
| Roles and access control                    | free                                                                         | free (admin, member)                                                  | free (owner, admin, member); custom roles in Enterprise | basic in CE, RBAC paid                                                         |
| For agents                                  | an MCP server, a Claude Code plugin, tokens limited to one sandbox           | an MCP server (`/mcp`; read-only at first, deploys in later releases) | an MCP server (`Dokploy/mcp`, also deploys)             | none built in                                                                  |
| A preview per pull request                  | not yet ([roadmap](https://csakaszamok.github.io/p9m/0.18/roadmap/index.md)) | yes (GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket, Gitea)                                | yes (GitHub)                                            | no                                                                             |

On a shared Docker daemon, anyone who may deploy an arbitrary compose file can, for example, bind-mount host paths or attach to another project's network: the separation in the dashboard does not reach the daemon.

**They work well together:** try and build in a Purgatorium sandbox, push the image to its registry, run it in production with Coolify or Dokploy. A Purgatorium sandbox can also have its own Portainer (the `portainer` template), for that sandbox's daemon alone.

## Looks similar, does a different job

These come up in the same searches ("sandbox", "dev environment", "AI agent"), but they solve another problem:

- **Coder, GitHub Codespaces, Gitpod / Ona, DevPod:** a workspace for **writing code** (an IDE, a repo, a terminal), not a place where the finished app keeps running for others. They fit next to Purgatorium: write in Coder or on the laptop, run in Purgatorium. Coder also runs coding agents: **Coder Tasks** starts one (Claude Code among them) in a workspace of its own, which pauses when idle, and **Coder Agents** runs its own agent from the control plane, so the model's keys never enter the workspace; process-level network and command rules for agents (Agent Boundaries) are not in the free edition. What the agent builds lives as long as its workspace, without an address for colleagues.
- **E2B, Daytona, Docker Sandboxes, Modal, Northflank sandboxes, kubernetes-sigs/agent-sandbox, Alibaba OpenSandbox:** they let an agent **execute code** in an isolated box for minutes or hours, driven from an SDK, usually inside a microVM. None of them is meant to keep a team's app online at a URL for weeks. Daytona is no longer open source: its development moved to a private codebase, and its AGPL repository is archived at v0.190.0 (a community fork, Nightona, carries it on).

## Where Purgatorium is weaker

1. **Isolation is not yet a boundary against hostile code.** The `dind` runtime runs the sandbox `privileged`: root inside a sandbox can escape to the host. That is fine for colleagues and their own agents, not for strangers. The `sysbox` runtime removes `privileged` and is used in production, but still shares the host's kernel; a **Kata Containers** runtime, a lightweight VM with its own kernel per sandbox, is on the [roadmap](https://csakaszamok.github.io/p9m/0.18/roadmap/index.md).
1. **One host for now.** No multi-host scheduling and no warm pool; a new sandbox takes about 10 seconds once its images are pulled (the first one on a new server a minute or two), a wake from deep sleep about 30. **Kubernetes support** is on the roadmap.
1. **Sleep stops the containers.** On wake the stack restarts by its restart policies; what was only in memory is gone.
1. **Missing pieces:** no teams yet (a sandbox has one owner), no hard disk quota (only a warning above a disk limit; CPU and memory limits exist), no egress rules, no SDK (a REST API with an [OpenAPI document](https://csakaszamok.github.io/p9m/0.18/api/#openapi-and-clients) to generate a client from, the Docker CLI and [agent-guide.md](https://csakaszamok.github.io/p9m/0.18/agent-guide/index.md)).
1. **A young, small project:** no community yet, no external security audit.

## When to choose something else

- **Production that must scale and stay up without you** → a cloud PaaS, or Coolify / Dokploy on your own servers.
- **Untrusted code from strangers** (public sign-up) → a microVM sandbox (E2B, Docker Sandboxes, Northflank), until Purgatorium has a Kata runtime.
- **Writing code in a cloud IDE** → Coder or Codespaces.
- **An agent running short scripts from an SDK** → E2B, Daytona (as a service) or agent-sandbox.
- **Coding agents for a large engineering team, with policies per process** → Coder (its agent features beyond Tasks are partly paid).
- **GPU or ML work** → Modal.
